title: Employment Situation, January 2027 (BLS, 08:30 ET)
source: EST: derived from BLS's own published scheduling rule as re-implemented and re-validated by the jobs-2027-08-06 initial research on this calendar — the Employment Situation is released on the third Friday following the end of the reference week (the Sun-Sat week containing the 12th). For January 2027 data the reference week is Sun 2027-01-10 to Sat 2027-01-16, and the third Friday after 01-16 is 2027-02-05, an ordinary NYSE session with no holiday within a week of it (Presidents Day is 2027-02-15), so the rule's one documented failure mode — a holiday landing on the rule's own Friday — cannot fire. Cross-checked against the publisher this session: bls.gov/schedule/news_release/empsit.htm fetched direct 2026-09-09 returned HTTP 200 (55,578 bytes) from this runner rather than the 403 recorded as a standing blind spot in docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md, but it publishes the 2026 schedule only — its 12 dated rows run Jan. 09, 2026 through Dec. 04, 2026 and there is no 2027 panel; bls.gov/schedule/news_release/2027_sched.htm and bls.gov/schedule/2027/home.htm both returned HTTP 404. So the prefix stays EST:: the rule is BLS's, the 2027 date is this lane's arithmetic, and no primary names it. Discovered 2026-09-09 in the never-assessed initial research of treasury-refunding-2027-02-03
notes: PROPOSED because this calendar has a gap in the jobs-* series between jobs-2026-12-04 and jobs-2027-05-07 (itself a proposal), and this entry sits inside the February 2027 refunding corridor at D+2 from treasury-refunding-2027-02-03 (est). It matters for that corridor specifically: the refunding week already carries two same-or-adjacent-session collisions — ism-manufacturing-2027-02-01 (high) on the Monday and ism-services-2027-02-03 (high) 90 minutes after the 08:30 ET announcement on the Wednesday — and a payroll print on the Friday means no bond move anywhere in that week can be attributed to the supply announcement on the tape alone. That attribution problem is the one treasury-refunding-2026-11-04's ledger caught retroactively for 2026-08-05, generalised here into a rule. Impact HIGH matches every other jobs-* entry on this calendar. CARRIED, NOT VERIFIED THIS SESSION: the January Employment Situation is also the edition that normally carries the CES annual benchmark revision and updated household-survey population controls, which would make it the highest-content payroll print of the year — bls.gov/web/empsit/cesbmart.htm fetched HTTP 200 but is a methods article rather than a timing statement, and the 2026 benchmark notice returned 404, so that characterisation is carried from standing BLS practice and is not sourced here; it is not load-bearing for the proposal, which stands on the date rule and the corridor position alone. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
